prediction.null_direction: no end-to-end coupling OR reversed sign at any link
prediction.calibration_source: IAEA Fukushima Daiichi final accident report (2015); METI Japan Strategic Energy Plan revisions; TEPCO public dispatch data 2010-2012. All public.

kill_condition.rule: fail if slope < 0.20 (chain too weak — recovery does not transit substrate boundaries), fail if slope > 0.75 (over-prediction beyond IAEA/METI window), fail if slope < 0 (null direction realized at chain endpoints)
kill_condition.rationale: The voice claims a positive, bounded chain coupling across three substrate boundaries. End-to-end measurement is the cleanest test of the chain claim and is testable from run output alone. The null direction is named explicitly per §3.2.

input_parameters.scenario_descriptor: Six nuclear-capacity-loss scenarios spanning pre-event (0.0) to documented post-event shutdown peak (~0.85, reflecting the share of Japan's nuclear fleet offline during 2012). Calibrated from TEPCO + METI.

verdict.rationale: Observed slope 0.5068 is within the pre-committed range [0.2000, 0.7500], calibrated from the IAEA + METI + TEPCO public sources. The methodology's chained-coupling protocol recovers the documented direction and magnitude across three substrate boundaries. Per §1 honesty bounds, this is not a real-economy measurement; the substrate is parameterized from the public reports.
